intro: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is in France for the Paris Peace Forum and is expected to travel to Turkey for the COP31 summit, while high-level talks with Iran focus on regional connectivity and the TRIPP initiative. Meanwhile, the Armenian community in Glendale held a rally for Artsakh, and a criminal proceeding has been launched into a recent parliament brawl.

topics.title: Pashinyan attends Paris Peace Forum, plans Turkey trip for COP31
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has departed for France on a working visit to participate in the 9th Paris Peace Forum. Armenian and international sources confirm he is also scheduled to travel to Turkey later this week to attend the COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya.

topics.title: Armenia and Iran discuss regional connectivity and TRIPP assurances
topics.text: During a visit by Iran's Vice President to Yerevan, officials discussed bilateral cooperation, unblocking regional transit routes, and economic agenda items. Iranian officials stated Armenia provided assurances that the TRIPP initiative will not alter regional borders or geopolitics.

topics.title: Armenia, U.S., and Azerbaijan launch TRIPP planning groups
topics.text: CivilNet reports that Armenia, the United States, and Azerbaijan have launched planning groups for the TRIPP initiative. This development follows regional discussions on transport corridors and connectivity involving Armenian and Iranian leadership.

sources.title: Armenia, U.S., Azerbaijan launch TRIPP planning groups

topics.title: Glendale Armenian community holds Artsakh rally and vigil
topics.text: The Armenian community in Glendale united for a rally, silent march, and candlelight vigil in support of Artsakh. The event was covered by multiple diaspora-focused outlets, highlighting ongoing advocacy efforts.

topics.title: Criminal proceeding opened into Armenian parliament brawl
topics.text: Authorities have launched a criminal proceeding regarding the brawl that occurred in the Armenian parliament on October 29. The investigation follows the physical altercation between lawmakers during a heated session.

sources.title: Criminal proceeding launched into October 29 brawl in Armenia parliament

topics.title: Armenian nuclear plant to operate until at least 2035
topics.text: A government minister confirmed that Armenia's nuclear power plant will continue operating at least until 2035. The announcement addresses the country's energy security and long-term infrastructure planning.

sources.title: Armenia nuclear plant to continue operating at least until 2035, minister says

topics.title: Opposition launches campaign against Pashinyan's constitutional plans
topics.text: Armenian opposition forces have united against Prime Minister Pashinyan's proposed constitutional changes, launching a nationwide campaign. The move signals deepening domestic political tensions.

sources.title: Armenian Opposition Unites Against Pashinyan’s Constitutional Plans, Launches Nationwide Campaign
